questiontext.text:
A sound level meter measures the sound level of a machine as {@L@} decibels (dB). The sound level is modelled by \(L=10\log_{10}\left(\frac{I}{I_0}\right)\),

where \(I\) is the sound intensity in watts per square metre (\(\mathrm{W/m^2}\)), and \(I_0=10^{-12}\,\mathrm{W/m^2}\) is the reference intensity.

Calculate the sound intensity \(I\). Give your answer in \(\mathrm{W/m^2}\), using scientific notation where appropriate.

[[input:ans1]][[validation:ans1]][[feedback:prt1]]

generalfeedback.text:
Worked solution

The sound level is given by \(L=10\log_{10}\left(\frac{I}{I_0}\right)\), where \(I_0=10^{-12}\,\mathrm{W/m^2}\).

Step 1: Divide both sides by 10.

\(\frac{L}{10}=\log_{10}\left(\frac{I}{I_0}\right)\).

Step 2: Convert from logarithmic form to exponential form.

Using the identity \(\log_{10}(x)=y\iff x=10^y\), we obtain \(\frac{I}{I_0}=10^{L/10}\).

Step 3: Make \(I\) the subject.

Multiplying both sides by \(I_0\) gives \(I=I_0\,10^{L/10}\).

Step 4: Substitute the given values.

\(I=10^{-12}\times 10^{{@L@}/10}\,\mathrm{W/m^2}\).

Therefore, the sound intensity is \(I={@I@}\,\mathrm{W/m^2}\).
